newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech central bank sets three repo tenders.
newsitem.headline: Czech central bank sets three repo tenders.

text.p: The Czech National Bank (CNB) on Monday set a one-week repo tender with an unlimited rate, compared to a similar tender on Friday which had a rate of 12.9 percent.
The CNB added in a statement that it had also set two overnight repo tenders with a maximum rate of 45 percent.
The CNB added in the statement that the rate in the one-week tender would be determined by the bids.
Last Friday bank board member Ludek Niedermeyer told Reuters rates at central bank open market operations would be set by market conditions.
The CNB holds repo tenders to either supply or drain liquidity from the market almost daily.

Last week's announcement came after the crown plunged to a record low of five percent on the depreciation side of its dollar/mark basket parity on Thursday, prompting the CNB to intervene on the market to support the currency for the first time in over a year.
As part of its support package for the crown, the CNB also raised the Lombard rate to 50 percent from a previous 14 percent.
